summary: Preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes an undeclared, heavily obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package's package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs is an obfuscator.io-style script (opaque _0xNNNN identifiers, per-scope string-map dispatchers wrapping trivial calls) whose actual behavior is to download the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases (bun-v1.3.13, arch-specific zip), extract it (using unzip on Unix or Expand-Archive/powershell on Windows, with an /etc/os-release Alpine check), chmod the binary to 0755, then execFileSync the Bun binary against a sibling file math_init.js at install time. math_init.js is a 727KB Bun-compiled bundle (header '// @bun @bun-cjs') using string-array rotation obfuscation (WV8StW rotates the n7gIxM array), and is not listed in package.json files (which only exposes 'docs'), so it is shipped in the tarball but hidden from the declared file manifest. The advertised purpose is a documentation bundle for a UI kit; downloading a second JavaScript runtime at install time and using it to execute an undeclared, heavily obfuscated sibling bundle has no relation to that purpose and matches the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern, where the alien runtime is used to bypass Node-based static analysis of the executed payload. The package is published under the @servicetitan scope and points to github.com/servicetitan/uikit.git, but the contents are inconsistent with a legitimate first-party docs artifact, indicating scope impersonation.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
